### ① Derived judgments

- **M1, M2 on base — hold.** Own probe (base worktree at `704e05b09d`, real `FlowSimulator` → real `ScreenPreview`, under the verify lock). Console sample: `note` absent at the pause, still absent after typing `5`, `comment` drawn throughout; `buildScreenSpec(node, variables).fields` was `[discount, comment]` with no `visibleWhen` carried. Docs shape: `opportunityName` absent; after the tick (`data-state` checked) still absent; `plain` drawn; identical with `createOpportunity: false` seeded. The base step note read "Hidden because its visibleWhen could not be evaluated … `note` (Unknown variable: discount)". M2: `unevaluableVisibleWhen(node, variables)` on base named `note` and `opportunityName`; with `needsApproval: true` seeded it reported nothing and `Reason` was drawn; with `false` it reported nothing and `Reason` was hidden silently. Exactly the dev's reading.
- **One evaluator — partly.** Preview and Debug run both render through `ScreenPreview` → `ScreenView` (`visibleScreenFields`/`screenPredicateScope`); `screen-spec.ts` evaluates no value. Repo-wide grep at head for `fieldVisibility|isFieldVisibleWhen|evalVisibleWhen`: only the 10743 changeset text (the `FieldVisibilityDeclaration` hit in `ExpressionProvider.tsx` is form field rules, unrelated). `evalVisibleWhen`'s removal is safe: on main its only caller was `screen-spec.ts`; `evalGuard` and `evalBranchPredicate` still route through `evalCelPredicate` over `flowCelScope`, untouched. Parity-pin re-judging: every removed row pinned the Studio's own value evaluation over run variables, which the ruling abolishes; the replacement rows pin scope only. No drift; one CEL-semantics family (`size()`, `n == "2"`, `vars` control) retires with the evaluator whose subject is now `ScreenView`'s.
  ⛔ **A second scope judgement of the same key survives in `metadata-admin/previews/flow-expr-problems.ts`** (`checkCel` → `findUnknownRefs` over `resolveFlowScope`, the FLOW scope: upstream outputs, not the screen's own fields). Measured at head with an assignment upstream of the console-sample screen: Problems panel emits `warning "Note: \`discount\` is not a reference in scope at this step."` while the Debug-run step is silent; for `needsApproval == true` the Problems panel is silent while the step errors. Same code on base (measured: same warning), but on base both surfaces read the flow scope and agreed; this PR makes the Studio contradict itself on the only shipped producer shape. The inline inspector's `FlowObjectListField` receives the same flow `scopeGroups` for expression columns (`:282`), not rendered here.
- **Direction fence.** A faulting predicate is drawn at head (measured: `needsApproval == true` with the run holding `false` → `Reason` drawn, no hint; console sample with `discount` seeded `null` → `note` drawn, `hiddenFieldCount` 0, because `dyn null greater-than int` is a CEL fault and `evalFieldPredicate` falls open). Stated as a rebind to `ScreenView`'s fallback with objectui#8069 named, in the changeset, the dated note, `screen-spec.ts`, `flow-simulator.ts`. The Debug run names the fault on the step (`error`, drawn rose at `FlowSimulatorPanel:415`): "A screen field's visibleWhen may reference only the fields declared on this screen; the screen cannot evaluate "note" (`needsApproval` is not a field on this screen)." The inspector's standalone preview has no step, so a scope fault there is named nowhere (the Problems panel names the wrong shape, above). The 10692 dated note is true about what changed.
- **Scope rule.** `record` IS bound by the runner: `evalFieldPredicate(pred, scope, true, undefined, scope)` → engine `buildScope` binds `record` plus `extra` keys only; measured `record.discount == null` ok, and `vars`, `previous`, `input`, `os`, `user`, `current_user` all "Unknown variable" — so declared fields plus `record` is exactly the runner's binding. `record` is restated by hand (`RECORD_ROOT`), not read off `screenPredicateScope`, contrary to the docblock's "so the two cannot disagree". `collectCelRootIdentifiers` (formula 17.4.0): `size(tags)`, `has(record.x)`, string literals, ternary, `note.contains("x")` all fine; **comprehension variables are false-reported** — `["a","b"].exists(t, t == note)` → "`t` is not a field on this screen" while the runner evaluates it. No `ScreenView` field type yields a list, so only list literals reach it; unpinned, non-blocking. Typo row holds: `nearestName` cap is max(2, len/3) → `dicount` → `discount`, `needsApproval` → none; names of one or two characters always get a suggestion.
- **`hiddenFieldCount(spec, values)`.** Follows the renderer exactly (measured along null, 0, 5: count 0, 1, 0; hint absent, present, absent). `required` plays no part and the preview has no Submit.
- **Runner.** `ScreenView.tsx` diff: `export` on `screenPredicateScope` plus five docblock lines; zero behaviour change. Not on `src/index.ts` (no `export *`; the views block names `FlowRunner` and the types `ScreenFlowState`, `ScreenSpec`, `ScreenFieldSpec` only); README Export Check green. Clause-② no holds.
- **Pins.** Head, 7 files: `Test Files 7 passed`, `Tests 138 passed`. Base leg (head pins over `704e05b09d`): `24 failed | 35 passed (59)`, all three files red. Ablations over the 3 pin files, anchor hit once, blob restored equal to HEAD each time: A1 `8 failed | 51 passed`; A3 `8 failed | 51 passed`; A6 `5 failed | 54 passed`. No tautology; the run-variable render pin (`reasonWithFalse` equals `reasonWithTrue`) is weak alone but red on base and paired with the step-error pin.
- **Type-check** app-shell at head after the closure build (`Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`): `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exit 0.

### ② Semver level

- `patch`, `Clause-②: no`: confirmed (export question above; retired functions were never on the index).
- 10692 changeset: frontmatter md5 `4e8ce55021fe3b14329c8b4cb3f9f354` on both sides; dated note in the objectui#10533 form. Pending changesets naming touched files still hold: 10367 (`ScreenView` `aria-required`, behaviour untouched), 8526 (`ScreenPreview` renders `EmptyDescription`, line 83 at head), 10692 (note appended). No changeset-claim-re-read bot comment exists on the PR; the check run is green.
- Server claims against objectstack main `455dcc060d`: `refuseInvalidScreenInput` still builds `new Map(Object.entries(run.variables))` with the bag layered; `registerFlow`'s ledger arm still calls `check(slotWhere, found.value, false)` with no identifier set — the undeclared-identifier refusal does not exist, and no sentence in changeset, README, docblocks or PR body claims it does. Brace, non-string and blank refusals (`predicateSlotRefusal`, `validateExpression`) exist as stated.
- ⛔ **Overstatement, changeset last sentence and PR body Acceptance notes last bullet:** "while the server waives its `required`" / "its `required` waived by the server". `validateScreenInputs` enforces `required` whenever `visibility(field) === true`, so a run whose variable makes the predicate true has the server ENFORCE it. Replacement: "while the server enforces its `required` only when the run's variables make the predicate true, and waives it when they make it false or leave it unevaluable."
- Minor: `screen-spec.ts` docblock "it is closed on the server side" reads as done; write "it is to be closed on the server side".

### ③ Boundary flags

- CI on head: 43 runs — 39 success; 3 skipped by design (Test coverage, coverage shard, dependabot); Changeset Bump Policy reports status in_progress with conclusion success. All 8 test shards, dist pins, Type Check, Lint, README Export Check, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Changeset Declaration and Claim Re-read: success.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree` against current main `f308a655b8` (two commits past the PR base: #10753, #10708, neither touching the 11 files): clean, exit 0; PR `mergeable_state` clean.
- Open PRs: 12 others, file lists read (release PR 5400 over 5 pages): none touches the 11 files, `previews/`, `ScreenView.tsx` or `FlowRunner.tsx`.
- Governed predicate: `0 of 11 path(s)` governed, 846 lines under 5000, exit 0 — ordinary queue landing.
- Draft: true. Labels `documentation`, `tests`, `package: app-shell`; assignee `os-elon-musk`; card `pm:dispatched`.
- Dev's out-of-scope finding is real: `inspectors/flow-node-config.ts:743` placeholder `stage == "review"` sits on the `visibleWhen` column of the SCREEN node's `fields` objectList (`screen:` block from `:31`, help "Input fields collected on this screen") — the screen-field slot, a run-variable-shaped example the runner cannot bind. Not filed; it belongs on the same follow-up card as the Problems-panel scope.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-10743-screen-predicate-run-scope`
Reviewed-by: `session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Two items stop the landing: (1) `previews/flow-expr-problems.ts` still judges a screen field's `visibleWhen` over the flow scope, so at head the Studio's Problems panel warns on the sibling-field shape and stays silent on the run-variable shape — the inverse of the Debug-run step — which contradicts the ruling's "sibling-field predicate is not reported" and the PR body's unqualified "one client evaluator / diagnostics evaluate over the declared screen scope"; either amend the claim to include that file and derive the `fields[].visibleWhen` column's roots from `screenPredicateScope(buildScreenSpec(node), {})` plus `record`, or state the remaining divergence in the changeset, README and PR body and file the follow-up card. (2) The "server waives its `required`" sentence in the changeset and PR body is false whenever the run's variable makes the predicate true; use the replacement text above.
